title: Abstract algebra II: rings, fields and Galois theory
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Continue algebra with rings and fields: rings, ideals and quotient rings, prime and maximal ideals, polynomial rings and irreducibility, Euclidean, principal ideal and unique factorization domains, field extensions and degrees, splitting fields and finite fields, ruler-and-compass constructions, and the fundamental theorem of Galois theory with its classic consequences.
primary_reading: Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications by Thomas W. Judson (free online)

weeks.2: Ideals, quotient rings and ring homomorphisms
weeks.4: Fields of fractions and the characteristic of a ring
weeks.5: Polynomial rings and the division algorithm
weeks.6: Irreducibility tests: rational roots, reduction modulo a prime and Eisenstein
weeks.7: Euclidean domains, principal ideal domains and unique factorization
weeks.8: Field extensions, algebraic elements and degrees
weeks.11: Field automorphisms and the fundamental theorem of Galois theory
weeks.12: Solvability by radicals and the insolvability of the general quintic

blocks.deliverable: Find the ideals of a supplied ring and identify a quotient.
Prove that a quotient ring is a field exactly when the ideal is maximal.
Decide the irreducibility of supplied polynomials with proofs.
Week 7 midterm; compute the degree of a supplied field extension.
Construct a finite field of a given order and prove an impossibility result.
Compute the Galois group and the subfield lattice of a supplied polynomial.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Galois notebook: work out in full the Galois groups and intermediate fields of three polynomials (one with a cyclic group, one with group S3 and one biquadratic), implement arithmetic in a finite field of order p^n in plain Python and check that its multiplicative group is cyclic, and write a clear expository account of why the general quintic is not solvable by radicals.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
